description: Onion is a bulb vegetable grown in kharif, late kharif and rabi, mainly in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh and the Kurnool area of Andhra Pradesh. It is shallow-rooted and needs sulphur, good drainage and light, regular irrigation.
npk_split: Apply one-third of the N with all P, K and 30-45 kg sulphur/ha at transplanting, and the rest of the N in two equal splits at 30 and 45 days after transplanting.

Caterpillar.name: Caterpillar
Caterpillar.description: Caterpillars that scrape and bore into the hollow onion leaves and feed from inside. Young crops can be stripped quickly, and the feeding wounds let leaf diseases enter.
symptoms: White papery scraped patches on the leaves
Holes in the leaves with caterpillars feeding inside the hollow leaf
Leaves cut or eaten from the tip
Green to brown droppings inside damaged leaves
Caterpillar.spread: Moths lay egg masses on the leaves and the caterpillars move from plant to plant, feeding mostly at night.
Caterpillar.action: Collect and destroy egg masses and caterpillars, and spray emamectin benzoate 5 SG 0.4 g/L with a sticker in the evening if damage is spreading.

treatment.name: Emamectin benzoate 5 SG
treatment.notes: Add a sticker (0.5 ml/L) because onion leaves are waxy; spray in the evening; only where the label lists your crop.

treatment.name: Neem oil 1500 ppm
treatment.notes: For light damage or as the first spray on young caterpillars; add a sticker.

Fusarium basal rot.name: Fusarium Basal Rot
Fusarium basal rot.description: A soil-borne fungus that rots the roots and the basal plate of the bulb, in the field and later in storage. There is no cure once the base has rotted, so control depends on clean seedlings, rotation and drainage.
symptoms: Leaves turn yellow and dry from the tip downward
Plant wilts and pulls out of the soil easily
Roots rotted and pinkish-brown, few in number
Base of the bulb brown and soft, sometimes with white mould
Bulbs rot from the base in storage
Fusarium basal rot.spread: The fungus lives in the soil for many years and spreads with infected seedlings, sets, soil and irrigation water, favoured by warm, waterlogged soil.
Fusarium basal rot.action: Pull out and destroy the affected plants, improve drainage, and drench the affected patch with carbendazim 50 WP 1 g/L to slow the spread.

treatment.name: Carbendazim 50 WP
treatment.notes: Dip seedling roots before transplanting and drench affected patches; this protects healthy plants but does not cure rotted ones.

treatment.name: Trichoderma viride
treatment.notes: Mix with well-rotted farmyard manure and apply to the soil before transplanting.

treatment.name: Crop rotation
treatment.notes: Keep onion and garlic off the field for 3-4 years, plant on raised beds and avoid injuring bulbs at harvest.

Leaf blight.name: Leaf Blight
Leaf blight.description: A fungal blight of onion leaves and seed stalks caused by Stemphylium, and in the rainy season also by Colletotrichum. Leaves dry from the tip downward and bulbs stay small.
symptoms: Small yellow to orange flecks or streaks in the middle of the leaf, often on one side
Flecks grow into long spindle-shaped spots with pinkish margins
Leaves dry from the tip downward and look blighted
With Colletotrichum: pale sunken spots with black dots, twisted leaves and a long neck
Leaf blight.spread: Survives on crop debris and spreads by wind and rain splash in warm, humid weather with long leaf wetness.
Leaf blight.action: Spray mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g/L with a sticker at the first flecks and alternate with propiconazole 25 EC 1 ml/L every 10-15 days.

treatment.name: Mancozeb 75 WP
treatment.notes: Add a sticker (0.5 ml/L) because onion leaves are waxy; start from 30 days after transplanting in wet weather.

treatment.name: Propiconazole 25 EC
treatment.notes: Alternate with mancozeb at 10-15 day intervals; add a sticker; only where the label lists your crop.

treatment.name: Raised beds and drainage
treatment.notes: Grow kharif onion on raised beds with drip or furrow irrigation and avoid excess nitrogen.

Purple blotch.name: Purple Blotch
Purple blotch.description: The most common fungal disease of onion leaves and seed stalks in warm, humid weather. Leaves break at the blotches and dry, which reduces bulb size and seed yield.
symptoms: Small white sunken spots with a purple centre
Oval purple-brown blotches with a yellow halo and dark rings
Leaves and seed stalks bend or break at the blotch
Leaves dry from the tip downward
Purple blotch.spread: Survives on crop debris and seed and spreads by wind and rain splash in warm, humid weather; thrips injury makes it worse.
Purple blotch.action: Spray mancozeb 75 WP 2.5 g/L with a sticker now and alternate with tebuconazole 250 EC 1 ml/L every 10-15 days.

treatment.name: Mancozeb 75 WP
treatment.notes: Add a sticker (0.5 ml/L) because onion leaves are waxy.

treatment.name: Tebuconazole 250 EC (25.9% EC)
treatment.notes: Alternate with mancozeb at 10-15 day intervals; add a sticker.

treatment.name: Thrips control
treatment.notes: Keep thrips in check, because their feeding wounds let the fungus enter the leaf.

Viral disease.name: Viral Disease
Viral disease.cause: Virus complex: Iris yellow spot virus (thrips-borne) and Onion yellow dwarf virus (aphid- and bulb-borne)
Viral disease.description: Virus diseases of onion, mainly iris yellow spot carried by thrips and yellow dwarf carried in bulbs and by aphids. There is no curative spray; infected plants give small bulbs and seed stalks fall over.
symptoms: Straw-coloured spindle or diamond-shaped spots on leaves and seed stalks, sometimes with a green centre
Yellow streaks along the leaves
Leaves flattened, crinkled and drooping
Stunted plants with small bulbs; seed stalks bend and lodge
Viral disease.spread: Iris yellow spot is spread by onion thrips, and yellow dwarf comes through infected bulbs or sets and is spread by aphids.
Viral disease.action: Pull out and destroy badly affected plants and spray spinosad 45 SC 0.3 ml/L with a sticker to bring down thrips.
Viral disease.vector: Onion thrips (Thrips tabaci); aphids for yellow dwarf

treatment.name: Roguing and clean planting material
treatment.notes: No spray cures the virus; raise seedlings from true seed in a clean nursery and do not plant bulbs or sets from an affected crop.

treatment.name: Spinosad 45 SC
treatment.notes: Thrips control only; add a sticker and direct the spray into the leaf bases where thrips hide; only where the label lists your crop.

treatment.name: Neem oil 1500 ppm
treatment.notes: Use between insecticide sprays; blue sticky traps help to monitor thrips.

healthy.name: Healthy
healthy.description: The leaf shows no sign of disease, pest or nutrient problem. Keep up regular field scouting and balanced nutrition.
symptoms: Upright, uniform green tubular leaves with a waxy bloom
No spots, streaks, holes or tip drying
Steady new leaf growth
healthy.action: Continue weekly scouting for thrips and leaf spots, especially in humid weather.
